evidence: Single deployable unit with one main entry point (sshuttle/__main__.py) and clear separation of concerns
Packages are grouped by responsibility (client, server, methods, helpers, firewall, tests) but all co-located in one repo and import each other freely
Strong module boundaries: methods/ contains platform-specific firewall implementations (nat, pf, tproxy) with BaseMethod abstracting variation
Core modules (ssnet, helpers, options) act as shared utilities used across layers
No explicit external communication boundaries (e.g., no RPC, message brokers, or service discovery)
Minimal package count (2 packages, implied by setuptools) and shallow directory depth (3 levels) typical of monoliths
Fan-out (avg ~4.9) is moderate — indicating modular interdependence but no heavy cross-cutting or distributed coupling
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., client → helpers → server indirectly) may reduce testability and deployability flexibility
Platform-specific firewall methods are conditionally imported and inherit from a common base, which is good — but not enforced strictly enough to prevent drift
